counties.name: Beckham County
counties.readerDecision: Give school organizers arrival instructions they can share.
counties.rationale: St. Louis City and Cerro Gordo cover museum-group choices. This brief adds distribution beyond the organizer: the arrive-together condition must survive copied school instructions and reach separately travelling sponsors, with a concrete acceptance check.

counties.name: Blaine County
counties.readerDecision: Choose the group-camp arrangement before using a reservation link.
counties.rationale: Madison and Dent cover group use and reservation boundaries. The added project value is a sleeping-arrangement comparison tied to a different application channel from ordinary campsites, with a wrong-checkout test and distinct photo inventory.

counties.name: Bryan County
counties.readerDecision: Connect the collection a visitor wants to see with the day it is open.
counties.rationale: Madison and Henry cover public opening and museum arrangements. This adds floor-specific collection availability and a direct collection-page arrival test, requiring an inventory of exhibit labels and schedule links rather than a generic hours rewrite.

counties.name: Caddo County
counties.readerDecision: Change arrival preparation when the accommodation changes.
counties.rationale: Sioux and Wayne cover stay choices and amenities. This brief specifically tests a change of accommodation after an arrival plan exists, keeping class-specific check-in and site extras together. It adds a useful content substitution check beyond paraphrasing campground policy.

counties.name: Canadian County
counties.readerDecision: Describe the event layout before assuming the arena floor is ready.
counties.rationale: Davis and Howell cover facility setup and event requirements. The additional value here is a dirt-to-event-surface preparation question plus the adjacent pavilion’s different environment, providing specific photo, specification and combined-space acceptance checks.

counties.name: Carter County
counties.readerDecision: Plan key collection and caterer review before the event day.
counties.rationale: Warren, Webster and Adair cover venue inquiries and use conditions. This brief adds two chronological dependencies before event-day access: a business-day key handoff and approval before contracting an outside caterer, with explicit weekend and unapproved-vendor tests.

counties.name: Cherokee County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the float reservation separate from the overnight stay.
counties.rationale: Crawford ties floats to guest eligibility and included lunch; McDonald compares shuttle sequences; Allamakee separates owned equipment. This brief instead preserves two reservations across a multi-night stay and a day-specific float, with a season-status override and route-change arrival test.

counties.name: Choctaw County
counties.readerDecision: Separate public tours, private encounters and group requests.
counties.rationale: Woodford compares animal-related experiences and Audrain separates museum formats. This local project adds a specific group brief containing adult/child counts, purpose and expectations alongside a separately described observation-deck arrangement; its acceptance test checks that an education request survives the handoff.

counties.name: Cimarron County
counties.readerDecision: Separate the Black Mesa hike from the overnight campsite.
counties.rationale: Wood and Fayette already explain activity-specific entrances; Tama distinguishes outdoor and building access. This brief adds separate facilities roughly fifteen miles apart, an overnight prohibition at the hiking destination and an itinerary test that prevents campsite confirmation from implying preserve access.

counties.name: Cleveland County
counties.readerDecision: Choose the food arrangement separately from exclusive pool use.
counties.rationale: Emmet distinguishes a private room from shared recreation, and Davis covers event-space preparation. This case adds exclusive waterpark use with excluded concessions and two mutually different food/payment arrangements, giving the owner a specific accounting-label inventory and switch-option test.

counties.name: Coal County
counties.readerDecision: Ask whether the visitor is preserving old media or making a new recording.
counties.rationale: St. Louis County has detailed transfer-session timing and Cook addresses unfinalized discs. This brief does not repeat those unsupported specifics: it adds a task-level fork between preserving media and recording new audio at a local branch, with the owner supplying format and assistance information before publication.

counties.name: Comanche County
counties.readerDecision: Make the current visit plan take precedence during a building closure.
counties.rationale: Des Moines, Morgan and Madison cover changing museum access. The local value is a multi-year construction transition requiring a full page inventory, direct indoor-collection landing test and a separate education-confirmation route, while keeping projected reopening distinct from a booked date.

counties.name: Cotton County
counties.readerDecision: Determine whether the available local sources support a useful printing, museum-visit or park-use website brief.
counties.rationale: Texas/Madison already provides substantive printing limits and Missouri/Butler a detailed self-service versus assisted-copy decision. Walters sources provide neither equivalent local preparation detail nor a different supported project brief. Population is not used as a filter.

counties.name: Craig County
counties.readerDecision: Show the room configuration, surface and kitchen choice together.
counties.rationale: Grundy discusses an opened wall and Kossuth an optional kitchen. This local brief combines concrete/carpet room choices with a named partitioned pair and explicitly tests the acoustic claim, then carries that arrangement into kitchen and deposit preparation. It requires a specific image/configuration inventory rather than a renamed generic room page.

counties.name: Creek County
counties.readerDecision: Distinguish a museum visit from the Model T driving experience.
counties.rationale: Woodford and Audrain compare tour formats. This brief adds participatory driving with a license-presentation prerequisite, small-session enrollment and included museum admission; the acceptance check separates admission from participation without creating a public identity-upload flow.

counties.name: Custer County
counties.readerDecision: Plan the grade mix and lunch space alongside the guided visit.
counties.rationale: Callaway covers a single supervision ratio and subgrouping; Woodbury adds rotations and a second museum. This brief carries grade-dependent review and an internal lunch-space request through one school itinerary.

counties.name: Delaware County
counties.readerDecision: Separate a trail walk from a visit to the seasonal museum.
counties.rationale: The existing seasonal and grounds/interior cases establish the principle. The combined free daily trail, separately seasonal museum, and section-specific route description creates a useful local scope and three distinct checks.

counties.name: Dewey County
counties.readerDecision: Keep a larger party’s revised headcount attached to its approved pool time.
counties.rationale: Lampasas and Emmet cover request/payment and public/private scheduling. The incremental value here is the post-approval attendance change, working-day notice and staff resourcing handoff, with a concrete count-change check.

counties.name: Ellis County
counties.readerDecision: Identify the cattle service stage before discussing a delivery.
counties.rationale: Florida Madison explains consumer product/custom-harvest stages and processor handoffs. Pennsylvania Pike explains service differences among branches. The Ellis brief adds a producer’s choice among receiving, backgrounding, finishing and associated services before lot and timing review.

counties.name: Garfield County
counties.readerDecision: Keep supervision groups separate from an optional class’s capacity.
counties.rationale: The closest school pages cover booking and group thresholds. This brief specifically tests two simultaneous capacities—supervision group and educational class—and their relationship to payment preparation.

counties.name: Garvin County
counties.readerDecision: Describe the cabinet, countertop and millwork package before requesting an estimate.
counties.rationale: Johnston already covers cabinet/countertop scope. Additional value rests on the source’s commercial coordination across materials, shop drawings, fabrication and installation, with a revision-impact test rather than a renamed product list.

counties.name: Grady County
counties.readerDecision: Choose the building by event activity and support spaces.
counties.rationale: Existing venue comparisons cover setup and rental readiness. This brief makes the dirt-arena versus presentation/kitchen choice explicit and tests cross-building amenity leakage.

counties.name: Grant County
counties.readerDecision: Distinguish an identified feed order from a request for a supplementation discussion.
counties.rationale: Pennsylvania Pike explains branch-specific services and contact routes; it does not provide an order-versus-consultation structure. The Grant brief adds a named feed product versus specialist discussion, hay-sampling preparation and a bulk-delivery/fulfillment question, while leaving actual branch supply to staff.

counties.name: Greer County
counties.readerDecision: Show which sample preparation instructions apply before the drop-off.
counties.rationale: Missouri Worth distinguishes local-office and direct-laboratory submission, payment reference and results handling. The Greer brief instead makes sample material and an unknown requested test the first choices, then connects approved preparation to the county-office drop-off and payment step.

counties.name: Harmon County
counties.readerDecision: Ask staff for an outside title and use the local branch for pickup and return.
counties.rationale: Worth already supplies a complete sample/submission/payment workflow; uncertain destination wording adds no safe improvement to it. The fully inspected local library alternative repeats Monroe’s staff-managed outside-loan request, pickup and return responsibilities, with less detail and no extra distinct selection or preparation rule. Card-based resource labels alone do not support a fuller commissioning brief. NO_ADDITION is based on this substantive alternative and full comparison, not the Extension access/conflict alone. The conflict remains a discarded-lead limitation rather than an asserted resolved operating fact.

counties.name: Harper County
counties.readerDecision: Separate published yard capacity from space for a particular incoming lot.
counties.rationale: The closest cattle-related record concerns meat orders and processing. This capacity-versus-availability brief has a different reader, requested information and failure case. It also differs from Ellis’s service-stage selection.

counties.name: Haskell County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the rental option’s return time and arrival preparation together.
counties.rationale: The guide covers selected-product preparation; this case adds an explicit overnight exception to a general same-day return rule and restricted short slots. The local brief tests those branches together.

counties.name: Hughes County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the site’s utilities and approval method attached to the selected stay.
counties.rationale: Meigs handles site versus shared amenities, while Calhoun handles category and stay length. This brief connects distinct utility categories to checking the selected option’s provider label and actual approval status. The capture does not establish which current site, if any, uses a non-Instant Book path; the pending-state acceptance check is a proposed test.

counties.name: Jackson County
counties.readerDecision: A reader requests an unavailable book and needs to know who handles borrowing and return.
counties.rationale: The library alternative is substantive but does not add enough beyond Monroe’s full outside-loan request, renewal and return treatment to support a separate service page.

counties.name: Jefferson County
counties.readerDecision: Separate watching the sale from starting buyer registration.
counties.rationale: Florida Madison is about farm/processor stages, not buyer approval. Coles concerns live-sale claim allocation and Berkshire retained property, so neither replaces this local report/view/registration handoff. The complete approved-buyer guide already supplies the general account-versus-permission principle; no new guide is justified. A Waurika service brief adds the actual shared location selector and sensitive-registration boundary to a public-route audit, with a useful returning-user check and owner inputs.

counties.name: Johnston County
counties.readerDecision: A group distinguishes free museum admission from a reserved guided visit.
counties.rationale: The museum brief duplicates the complete group-visit records. The substantive Blue River alternative establishes area-specific access and camping restrictions, but the proposed general itinerary content supplies no additional owner inquiry or service workflow beyond the existing experience-choice and timed-booking guides. Henry is relevant only to the original museum-access candidate, not camping.

counties.name: Kay County
counties.readerDecision: Attach every guest limit to its room, setup or package.
counties.rationale: The closest venue pages discuss setup and included facilities. This source provides three different numerical scopes; the brief’s incremental value is preventing arithmetic or substitution across room, layout and package.

counties.name: Kingfisher County
counties.readerDecision: Explain what a combined admission includes and what is currently open.
counties.rationale: Texas Polk handles a full-site closure versus routine hours. The Chisholm requires partial-building status inside a combined-admission offer, plus structure-specific preparation. This is a distinct maintenance and acceptance check.

counties.name: Kiowa County
counties.readerDecision: Separate a school road-show request from a festival inquiry.
counties.rationale: Buchanan and Jefferson cover program choice and school logistics. This local brief concerns mobile delivery, school-versus-festival terms and host-site confirmation, rather than routing a group to a fixed venue.

counties.name: Latimer County
counties.readerDecision: Give each kind of stay its own arrival instructions.
counties.rationale: The existing departure and campground records explain meeting points and arrival responsibilities. This brief adds a stay-type decision that changes the first destination and the appropriate reservation link, with a practical check for a guest towing an RV.

counties.name: Le Flore County
counties.readerDecision: Explain what a kitchen includes for the selected accommodation.
counties.rationale: The Wayne and Floyd records already address equipment and lodging distinctions. The additional useful brief is a unit-specific meal-preparation inventory: the word kitchen alone must not copy group-camp equipment expectations into a cabin stay.

counties.name: Lincoln County
counties.readerDecision: Keep activity units and event requests separate.
counties.rationale: Emmet covers a reserved room versus shared activities and Johnson rental responsibilities. Route 66 Bowl adds a different commissioning problem: mixed game/person/credit units, separate shoes and a special session, carried into an event request without inventing a bundle. Distinct department hours and the activity priorities produce a concrete owner brief beyond the earlier short event form.

counties.name: Logan County
counties.readerDecision: Separate changing a ticket from arriving late.
counties.rationale: Hood and Macon cover live-performance timing and booking. This project combines the before-travel change route with the on-the-way late-arrival route while keeping exchange, transfer and admission decisions separate. The useful work is the navigation and policy handoff, not another generic showtime paragraph.

counties.name: Love County
counties.readerDecision: Describe the package unit before customers add their extras.
counties.rationale: The San Saba and experience-choice material distinguish products. This brief adds a bundled lodging-and-activity unit, where room count, party size and extra nights or rounds cannot be inferred from a package name.

counties.name: McClain County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the selected location attached to its opening days.
counties.rationale: Webster already addresses branch-specific meeting timing. This local brief concerns choosing an office before visiting, with location-specific opening days and phone routing rather than meeting-room start and cleanup buffers.

counties.name: McCurtain County
counties.readerDecision: Explain the trip conditions before asking for a preferred time.
counties.rationale: McDonald and Allamakee cover outfitter choices and participation conditions. This brief adds a two-part published participation condition before a preferred-time request, with an explicit distinction between a request and current operator confirmation.

counties.name: McIntosh County
counties.readerDecision: Show preparation and return times with the rental slot.
counties.rationale: Clay and Monroe cover marina and rental decisions. This brief adds the relationship among the selected block, advance lesson time and return, plus a specific supplied-versus-customer-provided preparation item. It is not a generic availability calendar.

counties.name: Major County
counties.readerDecision: Distinguish visiting hours from vehicle access.
counties.rationale: Louisa and the Missouri recreation records discuss access and visitor preparation. This brief adds transport-specific access windows and the lack of an overnight product, requiring the website to avoid converting a walking-hours label into a vehicle-access promise.

counties.name: Marshall County
counties.readerDecision: Route the visit to the right marina department.
counties.rationale: Clay and Monroe already cover rental and marina timing; Louisa addresses visitor access. This brief adds purpose-based department routing, the distinction between land and water fuel access, and a separate handoff to independent providers.

counties.name: Mayes County
counties.readerDecision: Understanding industrial capabilities before discussing a project.
counties.rationale: Use the existing industrial website planning guide; no local service draft is justified by these facts alone.

counties.name: Murray County
counties.readerDecision: Separate campus access, exhibits and arranged group visits.
counties.rationale: Story and Jefferson explain museum and group-visit choices. This brief adds free campus access alongside paid exhibits and arranged interpretation, so a group-size threshold does not become a claim that a guide or every attraction is included.

counties.name: Muskogee County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the overnight arrival separate from the activity visit.
counties.rationale: Emmet covers packaged activity distinctions and Dallas covers accommodation arrival. The added brief combines an overnight timetable with a separately ticketed daytime activity and its own purchase counter, without treating the lodging booking as activity admission.

counties.name: Noble County
counties.readerDecision: Make preparation visible before a school visit is requested.
counties.rationale: Jefferson and Story cover group admission and visit selection. This brief adds preparation before the visit and a distinct post-booking resource handoff, so an organizer can scope the commitment before choosing a date.

counties.name: Nowata County
counties.readerDecision: Deciding whether a museum visit or scheduled event fits a proposed trip.
counties.rationale: Retain existing museum and experience-choice guidance; do not turn historical event notices into a new county brief.

counties.name: Okfuskee County
counties.readerDecision: Check the season before treating a monthly stay as an available option.
counties.rationale: Calhoun separates long-stay areas and Benton seasonal amenities. The new draft connects the season with the availability of a monthly arrangement, placement and a later eligibility discussion, including a cross-season acceptance case and deferred evidence. The existing rental-fit guide handles the general principle; no new guide is needed. Exact cutoff and provider conflicts are not resolved by guessing and are excluded from definitive customer instructions.

counties.name: Oklahoma County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the soft hold and contract deadlines distinct.
counties.rationale: Wapello, Webster, Howard and Johnson address room plans, supplier responsibilities and venue options. None develops the competing trigger dates of a soft hold and an issued contract. The current confirmation guide supplies the general state distinction; the local service brief adds an explicit contested-hold example and stage-specific owner inputs without automating acceptance.

counties.name: Okmulgee County
counties.readerDecision: Separate the initial catering request from the guaranteed guest count.
counties.rationale: Caroline and Wapello cover menu/service/layout quoting, while Webster covers venue staff and outside catering. The new brief contributes a timeline for estimated and guaranteed headcounts, the consequence of no update and later reduction limits, with university/external group routing. The quote and confirmation guides cover the reusable form principle, so separate local commissioning content is justified without another general guide.

counties.name: Osage County
counties.readerDecision: Keep group admission and a guided visit as separate arrangements.
counties.rationale: Scott and Story cover group rates and museum visits. This brief adds the difference between paying-adult count, complimentary roles and an optional guided arrangement with its own lead time, useful for a coach organizer planning both admission and interpretation.

counties.name: Ottawa County
counties.readerDecision: Give a group lunch its own tour request.
counties.rationale: Adds a hosted meal on a theatre stage, a specific group threshold and a shared tour/meal request to the existing visit-type and room/program principles. The local brief explains what an owner must supply and how to test an undersized group.

counties.name: Pawnee County
counties.rationale: Chariton covers a quote paid before release, Saline staff-classified scope, Washington appointments, Bureau evidence and effort limits, and DeKalb donations versus commissions. Pawnee’s complete brief instead explains an existing Donate-labeled payment route conditional on knowing the amount. The useful local work is preparation plus uncertain-total clarification plus the payment boundary, not the already-covered ranch closure. Wise checks an existing file before purchase; Warren uses estimates and payment before delivery. These differ from the source’s known-amount conditional use of a Donate-labeled route. Morrison’s new draft concerns opposite billing sequences, not this uncertain-total decision.

counties.name: Payne County
counties.readerDecision: Separate event-planning assistance from the services being booked.
counties.rationale: Goes beyond a room/program combination by connecting hotel-use qualification, quotation gathering and a city-bound transport-coordination offer. The owner receives three distinct acceptance cases.

counties.name: Pittsburg County
counties.readerDecision: Keep indoor and outdoor vendor applications on their own routes.
counties.rationale: Adds an actual two-organization application handoff and annual outside-vendor file to the existing vendor-status framework. The brief is about maintaining correct routing, not repeating a generic booth checklist.

counties.name: Pontotoc County
counties.readerDecision: Make an audition inquiry different from a ticket question.
counties.rationale: The closest group and research records distinguish request purpose, but do not address performer submissions, audition scheduling and selection as different stages. The specific local workflow supports a service brief without a new general guide.

counties.name: Pottawatomie County
counties.readerDecision: Explain group registration even when admission is free.
counties.rationale: Adds the consequential free-admission-day registration and paid-guide distinction, plus the unguided-group rule, beyond ordinary school versus adult-group preparation.

counties.name: Pushmataha County
counties.readerDecision: Compare sleeping privacy before choosing a ranch stay.
counties.rationale: Extends existing cabin equipment and dining comparisons with open sleeping privacy and the distinction between occupancy capacity and base-rate party size in a local ranch inventory.

counties.name: Roger Mills County
counties.readerDecision: Plan the indoor visit separately from the battlefield trail.
counties.rationale: Adds a concrete indoor/outdoor itinerary and segmented walking-route description to the existing building-access principles. It supplies owner inputs and checks for businesses recommending this nearby attraction.

counties.name: Rogers County
counties.readerDecision: Choose school activities from the class size and grade.
counties.rationale: Adds activity-level group limits and maximum selection count to the general school-visit brief; the acceptance case is a larger class choosing a small-group activity.

counties.name: Seminole County
counties.readerDecision: Plan the field trip, lunch and funding as separate decisions.
counties.rationale: Combines a specific lunch time block, food-order cutoff and separate limited-funding application with useful owner commissioning checks. It exceeds the existing trip-versus-bus-funding explanation through the meal workflow.

counties.name: Sequoyah County
counties.readerDecision: Confirm the chosen tour’s starting point and walking expectations.
counties.rationale: Applies the existing departure-address guide to a local multi-start custom itinerary, with specific separation of the cabin’s own address and wider tour arrangements. The service brief adds a route-version and walking-condition commissioning check.

counties.name: Stephens County
counties.readerDecision: Keep the learning program attached to its school-year dates.
counties.rationale: Adds school-year curriculum windows and a missing-confirmation-packet fallback to the existing class goal/count/date preparation. The proposed checks address a lesson carried into the wrong term.

counties.name: Texas County
counties.readerDecision: Explain what changes when a library card needs renewal.
counties.rationale: Adds a returning-user service-continuity brief and recurring proof requirement to the existing initial applicant comparison; the acceptance check separates account expiry from item renewal.

counties.name: Tillman County
counties.readerDecision: Distinguish an ordinary museum visit from a special-event inquiry.
counties.rationale: The museum visit versus private event distinction is already substantially covered by the full venue and visit records. No additional facility-use detail supports a stronger locally grounded brief; the trail alternative does not justify inventing ordering policies.

counties.name: Tulsa County
counties.readerDecision: Choose the photography request from the intended use and setting.
counties.rationale: Adds student-project preparation and distinct open-hours/after-hours garden conditions to the existing snapshot-versus-specialist and property-approval guidance. This is a local commissioning brief, not a new universal photography rule.

counties.name: Wagoner County
counties.readerDecision: Choose the building and the rooms before requesting event space.
counties.rationale: Adds a two-building comparison and independently rented room combinations, with time and equipment checks, beyond a single hall’s entrance or a room/program bundle.

counties.name: Washington County
counties.readerDecision: Distinguish a lawn photo session from an interior appointment.
counties.rationale: Provides an interior-after-hours permission and furniture-use brief distinct from Tulsa’s garden session routing and the existing commercial-image examples.

counties.name: Washita County
counties.readerDecision: Check the museum visit arrangement and separate it from other attractions.
counties.rationale: A museum-appointment page or seasonal-pool request would restate existing guidance without a new owner input, acceptance test or consequential local distinction supported by the source. The decision is no addition on this evidence, not a claim that the county lacks businesses.

counties.name: Woods County
counties.readerDecision: Select the correct campus before requesting a tour.
counties.rationale: Campus identity and separate scheduling routes repeat the existing full location and date-specific records. A current exceptions page could be useful for that institution, but these facts do not support a materially distinct county service brief.

counties.name: Woodward County
counties.readerDecision: Compare event buildings by the work the event needs to do.
counties.rationale: Adds activity-dependent building choice across livestock, exhibition and training uses, including the limit of an electrical-fixture description. This is more specific than generic venue inclusion or capacity advice.

keywordSummary.scope: US estimates for exact phrase wording, not county-resident demand. Shared and overlapping phrase volumes are not summed. Missing and refresh-required fields remain unavailable; partial metrics retain their status. Keyword estimates do not establish source accuracy, page quality, Google approval or ranking eligibility.
keywordSummary.contentDecision: No title, body, service-page, FAQ or guide additions were driven solely by a keyword metric. All county dispositions retain their source, locality and complete-content review basis.
